name_ru: Чжу Цзи Си Ши Инь Я
processing: Little is documented for this tea. The name points to a bud-grade green, made by the usual fixing, shaping and drying of the class.
harvest_season: Spring, as is usual for bud-grade Zhejiang greens.
appearance_dry: Little is documented; 'silver bud' suggests downy, bud-heavy leaf.
appearance_liquor: Likely clear pale yellow-green, as with other bud-grade Zhejiang greens.
appearance_wet: Likely tender green buds, as is typical of this class.
taste_profile: Its taste is little documented; bud-grade Zhejiang greens are generally light, fresh and gently sweet.

brewing.notes: General advice for a bud-grade green: cooler water, a glass, and a short first steep.

vintage_note: What is usual for its class applies: sold as the current spring's harvest and best within the year. Nothing specific is documented on its grades or years.
description:
Xishi Yinya is a green from Zhuji in Shaoxing, the hometown traditionally given for Xi Shi, one of the four legendary beauties of ancient China, which explains the name. It appears in listings of Zhejiang's regional teas but very little has been written about it.

'Silver bud' suggests a downy, bud-heavy tea, though its method and standards are little documented. Zhuji as a whole makes needle, flat and strip teas in different parts of the county.

If you meet it, brew it as you would any bud-grade spring green: cooler water and a short first steep. Those are habits for the class rather than anything recorded about this tea.

Do not confuse it with Xishi Shijian, a separate and better-documented Zhuji tea with its own standard. Ask the seller which one you are holding.
history: Little is documented. It is named in a listing of provincial origin teas as Zhuji's own, with no dates or makers given. Its link to Xi Shi is one of place and name, and nothing suggests the tea itself goes back to her.
